It boggles me that they don't grasp what makes indie games successful. How could they flip out on us for for not buying their game, when so many independent games in the last few years have been really successful? If there's nothing compelling about the gameplay or the story, there's no reason for it to be a game. It's not like no other small studios have made successful games with relatively simple gameplay that are still capable of telling interesting stories, it doesn't require a multi-million dollar budget. It's not revolutionary to try and just tell a story through some mild interactivity, that's like thinking you're bringing something to the media of film by having a short movie that's just a black screen and dialogue -- you're just misusing it and trying to conflate inability with creativity. Besides, if it was a really compelling story then people would be willing to give more leeway about the mechanics and gameplay anyway. When you botch both of those, how is it at all surprising that the game tanked? Obviously critical reception is worthless if actual gamers aren't interested in it. They made a decidedly mediocre piece of story-software and didn't manage the business aspects of the venture well. Surprise, when a person doesn't do anything well, the end result is not being lavished with rewards. Expecting otherwise is a weird mish-mash of entitlement, a lack of self-awareness, myopia, etc.

Also, has anyone noticed how they very clearly just aped their name from Telltale, a relatively popular publisher that tends to focus on story-driven adventure games? Was that supposed to be some kind of homage or are they just really so oblivious to think that no one would put that together?
Guess they should have made good games instead of "artistic" games with a message.

Maybe they should have made a game that gamers want to play and not paid someone who wrote an article called "Gamers are dead. Gamers don't have to be your audience anymore" to consult them on what people who play games might buy.

That's a small clue that made me think that maybe they were making games for a vociferous audience that does not actually exist.
